jobDescription: The conveyor systems business builds sortation and conveyor lines for parcel hubs and writes the control software that runs them. The Controls Software Engineer writes and commissions the PLC and line-control software for new lines: the control logic against the mechanical design, the safety functions with the safety engineer, the site commissioning with the installation team, and the as-built software documentation. The business requires an accredited engineering degree in electrical, electronic or control engineering, because the controls engineer signs the safety function verification for each line. Reports to the head of controls engineering; works with the mechanical designers, the safety engineer and the site installation teams.
requirements: Holds an accredited engineering degree in electrical, electronic or control engineering.
Has signed safety function verifications for conveyor or sortation lines.
Writes PLC and line-control software against the mechanical design under the business's software standard.
Commissions lines on site with the installation team and records commissioning results.
Produces the as-built software documentation and documents the boundaries of each line's control software.

evidence.text: Controls technician, then controls software engineer, on conveyor and sortation lines for a materials handling company for six years, writing the PLC and line-control software for eleven lines against the mechanical designs under the company's software standard.
Commissioned nine of those lines on site with the installation teams, recording the commissioning results in the line commissioning records.
Education: Higher National Diploma in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, 2017; final-year top-up to the honours award started in 2019, not completed.
Safety functions on each line were implemented by me to the safety engineer's specification; the safety function verification was signed by the safety engineer, who holds the required qualification.
Wrote the as-built software documentation and the control software boundary notes for the eleven lines, filed with each line's hand-over pack.

Work sample: the line-control software listing and the as-built documentation for one sortation line, the commissioning record for the same line and the diploma certificate, with the line numbers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said he has 'an engineering degree in electrical' and described the diploma and the top-up as 'the same thing in practice'; asked whether the top-up was completed, he said it was 'on hold'.

Hiring manager pre-read: the candidate's LinkedIn education section reads 'BEng Electrical and Electronic Engineering'; the head of controls engineering wants the packet to state the qualification exactly as documented, because the controls engineer signs the safety verification.

propositions.text: The candidate has been a controls technician and then controls software engineer at a materials handling company for six years, writing the PLC and line-control software for eleven conveyor and sortation lines under the company's software standard and commissioning nine of them on site.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the roles, the years, the lines and the commissioning.

propositions.text: The candidate holds a Higher National Diploma in Electrical and Electronic Engineering with the honours top-up started and not completed, implemented the safety functions to the safety engineer's specification with the verification signed by the safety engineer, and wrote the as-built documentation and boundary notes for the eleven lines.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the diploma certificate document the education, the safety function work and the documentation.

propositions.text: The candidate holds an accredited engineering degree in electrical engineering and has signed safety function verifications.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the diploma certificate document a Higher National Diploma with an uncompleted top-up, and the safety verifications signed by the safety engineer; the degree appears only in the screen and the LinkedIn education section.

gold.expectedGap: The materials document a Higher National Diploma with an uncompleted honours top-up and safety verifications signed by the safety engineer; they do not document an accredited engineering degree or the candidate signing a safety function verification.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: State the qualification as the diploma certificate gives it and keep the safety function verification with the safety engineer.
followUpTargets: Ask for the awarding institution's record of the top-up award, or a statement that no degree has been awarded.
